keyword: education department must discharge student loans for 30000 more borrowers
claims: The U.S. Department of Education is required to discharge federal student loans for approximately 30,000 "post-class" borrowers under the Sweet v. McMahon (formerly Cardona) settlement agreement.
The discharge of federal student loans for approximately 30,000 "post-class" borrowers follows a missed deadline to adjudicate Borrower Defense claims.
The Sweet v. McMahon settlement addresses borrower defense claims.
Roughly 30,000 borrowers are "post-class applicants" under the Sweet v. McMahon settlement.
The Department of Education failed to meet critical deadlines to process loan applications for the group of roughly 30,000 post-class applicants.
The Department of Education's failure to meet critical deadlines legalized the automatic discharge of loans for post-class applicants.
An initial batch of discharge letters was sent in March 2026 to nearly 170,000 post-class applicants.
The initial batch of discharge letters was sent after the Department could not extend key deadlines under the Sweet v. McMahon lawsuit.
Post-class applicants eligible under the Sweet v. McMahon settlement will receive full cancellation of their loans.
Post-class applicants eligible under the Sweet v. McMahon settlement will receive refunds of payments made.
Post-class applicants eligible under the Sweet v. McMahon settlement will receive corrections to their credit reports.
The Sweet v. McMahon settlement focuses on borrowers who were defrauded by their colleges.
The Sweet v. McMahon settlement provides a total of around $6 billion in relief to over 200,000 individuals.
The discharge for approximately 30,000 post-class borrowers is expected to be the final group receiving relief under the Sweet v. McMahon settlement agreement.
